newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TNT and Toll in rail freight j/v.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TNT and Toll in rail freight j/v.

text.p: TNT Ltd and fellow Australian transport group Toll Holdings Ltd said on Monday they had signed a heads of agreement to form a consortium to operate rail freight linehaul services throughout Australia.

In a joint statement the companies said the first objective of the consortium would be to expand the size and frequency of the current TNT service on the Melbourne - Perth corridor. TNT commenced its Melbourne-Adelaide-Perth service in July.
"The consortium will progressively seek to explore opportunities to commence operating rail linehaul services on other corridors," the companies said.

TNT said its Melbourne to Perth service was already exceeding expectations and customers were benefiting from improvements in service standards since the entry of TNT and the commencement of competition on the East/West corridor.

The companies said the Australian government's decision to divest its interests in rail and to establish a framework for a privately operated national rail system provided a significant impetus to TNT and Toll's intentions to form the consortium.

"Establishing a firm timetable for setting up a national independent track management authority by June 1997 is a vital element of the rejuvenation of the rail system," said TNT's managing director David Mortimer.
Mortimer said the private sector could not make long term investments in rail until it had a national uniform pricing regime for access to Australia's rail track network.
Mortimer said TNT and its partner encouraged the government to continue to push through its ambitious programme of rail reform so that more competitive services could be offered to customers.
TNT is the subject of a friendly A$2 billion takeover bid from Dutch post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN). Last Friday KPN said it had gained majority control.
